HN search interface useful: drop-down to sort results; feels like a faithful/predictable search engine vs Google's blackbox approach.
Complaint: searching HN via Google (site:news.ycombinator.com) gives better, more relevant results than the built-in Algolia-powered search, e.g. for 'ml' query.
DocSearch program for open source projects praised as 'really great'; Jekyll docs instant results usually find just what you want.
Algolia has great analytics, so you can measure business value from search queries: tie a query to a purchase and run further analysis, powerful without needing exceptional engineering talent.

Company switched from Algolia to ElasticSearch: 'Algolia is great to get started but it doesn't make sense at scale. If you have large indexes it's just too expensive.' Cited price and closed-source license as reasons.
'It's easy to use and setup. If pricing and closed source is OK with you then it's worth it.' Compared to pre-docker Heroku.
Typesense maintainer: 'Algolia is a great product but can get quite expensive at even moderate scale. If I had a dollar for every time I've heard this from Algolia users switching over…'
'We moved to Algolia mainly because of this [speed]. Elastic Search and Solr could not compete.' Algolia's RAM-first index approach cited as enabling much faster search-as-you-type than ES/Solr.

Competitor (Loop54) claim: customers switch from Algolia because 'Algolia requires a bit of hand-holding and it still doesn't quite seem to get what users are really looking for,' though Algolia has more tooling/knobs.

'Using them for a side project. Very impressed with their developer experience. Their React instant-search plugin is great, and very easy to add. Their documentation is great. Their admin UI is great.'

'We're currently A/B testing TypeSense and Algolia, but the pricing model difference alone makes me almost want to skip the whole process and just go with TypeSense. Algolia's price per search model is a little ridiculous for people building UIs with live search.'
Comparing to Typesense, a user noted 'One of Algolia's strongest features is InstantSearch for vanilla JS, React, Vue, Angular, iOS and Android' as a high bar to match.
'If you've ever tried installing ElasticSearch and then switched to Algolia you'll understand how great of a product it is.'
'I definitely love the hn search which is powered by algolia. Fast and instant. I wish it was possible to turn off fuzzy matching in some cases.'

'We're using Algolia (the free version) for all Facebook open source project websites (React, GraphQL, Yarn...) and it's been nothing short of awesome... It has required 0 maintenance, it didn't go down, the api didn't change.'
'Just their typo acceptance alone makes Algolia, imo, the best 3rd party search service available currently.'

Complaint about relevance: searching 'lipo' on an electronics site, 'the results start out promising... but by the time we get to the end of page 1, only every other result or so is actually relevant... fall off very rapidly into partial gibberish.'
'My only complaint, if I had to make one, is that pricing is a bit steep for our use case but I can't imagine how much time I'd need to spend to get ElasticSearch running comparably.'

'Algolia is an amazing service and an absolute joy to use... However, it's easy to exceed their record limits, especially since you need to duplicate your index every time you want to sort by something' — sorting by date/price requires extra slave indexes, quickly multiplying record usage (30K records became 150K).
'I miss the old HN search. The new one has some nice features, but it's missing basic search engine commands' like boolean OR queries.
